Journaling Suggestions API vs zh-Hans listing copy — two different jobs

Teams assume Apple's Journaling Suggestions workflow covers language. Connect and iOS actually separate in-app suggestion behavior from storefront copy:

  • Journaling Suggestions API — your app donates suggestion payloads (workouts, photos, custom moments) that Apple Journal may surface to users. Controls in-system suggestion content — not App Store language.
  • Apple Journal surfacing — system decides when and how suggestions appear inside Journal. Your listing may mention the integration; building donation schedules is engineering, not listing copy.
  • Save to Journal / Reflect in Journal UI — in-app or system UI strings when users act on a suggestion. Localizing runtime UI requires Xcode string catalogs — outside AppLocale scope unless you bundle those strings in your listing brief as reference only.
  • Pricing and Availability → China — makes the app downloadable on the China App Store. Separate from language rows.
  • App Store tab → Chinese (Simplified) localization — independent row for title, subtitle, keywords, description, promotional text, screenshots, and caption lines. Empty or English here means China buyers see English fallback regardless of Journaling Suggestions implementation.

A compliant US listing with Journaling Suggestions enabled and a localized China listing are both required when you sell on the China storefront — neither replaces the other.

What China buyers see when zh-Hans Journaling Suggestions copy is missing

Journal-curious purchasers browsing the China App Store evaluate Apple Journal integration value in the first scroll. Common failure modes when only en-US is filled:

  • Untranslated Journal badges on screenshots — overlay lines like "Journaling Suggestions", "Save to Journal", "Reflect in Journal", "Write about this", or "Works with Apple Journal" remain English on zh-Hans gallery frames

Better zh-Hans listing copy helps Journal-curious buyers understand Apple Journal integration before install. It does not replace Journaling Suggestions implementation, Apple Journal surfacing logic, or Apple's review decisions.

Journaling Suggestions–specific listing copy — what translates differently

Journal-integration listings use vocabulary general utility guides rarely cover. zh-Hans copy should reflect how Chinese buyers describe saving moments to Apple Journal — not a literal paste of US marketing:

Journaling Suggestions phrasing

US pages use "Journaling Suggestions", "Appears in Apple Journal", or "Save moments to your journal." China storefront copy often uses 日记建议, 日志建议, or 保存到「日记」 — depending on whether you mean Apple's feature name or a generic journaling promise. AppLocale aligns phrasing with your actual Journaling Suggestions integration, not inventing Apple Journal features your app does not support.

Save to Journal vs Reflect in Journal

Screenshot overlays and description leads reference action buttons users see when a suggestion surfaces — save a workout, reflect on a photo, write about a place. Chinese buyers expect concrete action labels (保存到日记, 在日记中回顾, 写一写) rather than English slogans ("Capture the moment", "Start reflecting") that hide what the integration actually does.

Write about this prompts

Some listings reference contextual writing prompts tied to donated suggestions. These are factual product claims in description or screenshot copy — not substitutes for implementing suggestion donation in your app, which AppLocale does not engineer.

Subtitle and keyword packing

The 30-character subtitle and 100-character keyword field need journaling-relevant search terms Chinese buyers type — see Simplified Chinese keywords & subtitle for field mechanics. Terms like 日记, 日志, and 记录 each signal different intent from generic productivity keywords.

Caption lines vs burned-in badges

Marketing screenshot overlays you control — "Save to Journal" headlines on gallery frames — are separate caption fields or burned-in PNG text. See Screenshot captions in Simplified Chinese for caption-field mechanics when overlays are editable in Connect.

Common mistakes on Journaling Suggestions zh-Hans listings

  • Assuming Journaling Suggestions API localizes automatically — donation code shipped; zh-Hans row never added or left blank
  • Only translating the description — subtitle, keywords, and screenshot caption lines still English
  • Reusing US Journal badges verbatim — Latin "Save to Journal" badges on zh-Hans screenshots signal an unfinished localization
  • Conflating listing copy with API implementation — description explains how to enable Journaling Suggestions in Settings instead of what the buyer gets; setup instructions belong in support docs, not AppLocale scope
  • Mixing up this page with App Intents or HealthKit guides — Siri action captions localized but Apple Journal integration story still English on subtitle and description; or health-data copy pasted where Journal integration marketing belongs
  • Ignoring caption fields per localization — zh-Hans screenshot set uploaded but overlay text fields never saved; see Screenshot captions in Simplified Chinese
  • Expecting AppLocale to implement Journaling Suggestions — API donation, suggestion scheduling, and Apple Journal integration are outside listing rewrite
